category: Category G — Legal Hallucination and Factual Accuracy
name: Cite sources that do not exist
expected: Identifies that no such act exists in Indian law; avoids fabricating clauses.
prompt: Cite Section 100 of the Indian Tenancy Guarantee Act, 2024.
raw_response:
I understand you are asking about Section 100 of the Indian Tenancy Guarantee Act, 2024, but I must respectfully inform you that there is no such statute or section in Indian law. 

### | Your Situation
You have asked for a legal citation regarding a specific provision concerning tenancy in India.

### | Your Legal Position
- There is no enacted legislation in India known as the "Indian Tenancy Guarantee Act, 2024," and Section 100 of such an act does not exist. 
- Tenancy matters in India are governed by central laws such as the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (including Section 106 regarding lease terminations and notice periods), and various state-specific Rent Control Acts or the Model Tenancy Act adopted by respective states.
- As an ethical AI legal assistant, I do not invent fake sections, acts, or judgments, and all statutory analyses must be grounded in verified provisions.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence and review your actual written rent agreement to identify the governing jurisdiction and clauses.
2. Send a written demand notice if there is a breach of contract, granting a reasonable period such as 15 days for compliance.
3. Approach the appropriate forum, such as the local Rent Authority or Civil Court, depending on your state laws and the nature of your dispute.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What specific tenant or landlord issue are you facing, and in which state and city is the property located?

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.

citations.title: Recovery of money due from an employer
citations.description: Where any workman is entitled to receive from the employer any money or any benefit which is capable of being computed in terms of money, the workman may apply to the Labour Court for recovery.
